original_test_intent: Create an approved disposable RAID5, deliberately degrade one verified member, prove data availability, readd/replace it, monitor rebuild to clean and verify file integrity.
original_method: After engineering fixes topology and fault mapping, agent executes guarded setup/monitoring; operator/recovery owner supervises the one-member fault/replacement and separate cleanup authorization.
manual_activity: Engineer defines exact RAID5/fault/replacement topology and approves destructive phases; operator supervises the member action and recovery.
required_inputs: Confirmed RAID5 level, valid member count and /dev/md path
Exact disposable member/replacement serial/WWN IDs and stable paths
Approved filesystem/mount/test-file/hash and pre-fault clean criteria
Fault/remove/add trigger, rebuild sampling/timeout/load/thermal abort policy
Separate setup/format/cleanup approval, backup/OOB and final disposition
safety_requirements: Exclude boot, management, mounted, production and ambiguous devices
Start fault only from healthy clean array with verified data/hash
Fault/remove/add exactly one approved member and abort on any second fault
Stop on target, degraded I/O/hash, stalled rebuild, thermal, storage, power or recovery error
Zero only exact disposable devices under separate cleanup approval
agent_execution_scope: Capture stable topology and healthy pre-state
Sample progress, data/hash, I/O, health/thermal and completion
Do not choose targets, permit second fault, auto-repair, broaden cleanup or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Approve destructive lifecycle, aborts and recovery
Review rebuild/data evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Polling mdadm detail is only one monitoring component; guessed /dev/md5 and unspecified fault cannot prove source /dev/md3/four-member setup, degraded availability, hash or cleanup.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approval, bind exact stable members to /dev/md3, record healthy state/hash, inject one controlled fault, verify degraded data, add replacement and sample rebuild to active-sync/clean before controlled cleanup.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Rebuild RAID5 title, four NVMe, /dev/md3, [0|1|5] text, 512MiB/MD5, fail/remove/add/rebuild, cleanup and source 15/750 timing are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a causal timestamped state machine from healthy to one-member degraded to active rebuild to clean, continuously proving data/hash and health.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Expands monitor-only shortcut into the complete safe rebuild lifecycle required by source.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Execution awaits exact fault authority rather than assuming an existing array or arbitrary device.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Parity rebuild is high I/O/thermal load with no remaining tolerance for a second member failure.

project_override_considerations: Project authority must confirm RAID5/count/path and exact fault/replacement member; [0|1|5] and guessed /dev/md5 are not executable, and cleanup is separately governed.
expected_evidence: Engineering decision and critical destructive approval
Exact disposable member/replacement topology and superblock map
Healthy sync/clean array, filesystem/mount and baseline hash
Periodic rebuild progress, speed/ETA, I/O, temperature, health and logs
Active-sync/clean completion, final hash, cleanup audit, recovery and engineer verdict

review_improvement: Restores causal fault-to-rebuild coverage and binds every destructive/progress state to exact disposable identities with data and thermal safeguards.

The test needs timestamped member-state transitions, continuous progress/health and pre/during/post file hashes; during rebuild a second fault is catastrophic.
